title: feat: WP11_BACKEND_USB_FLASH encrypted keystore backend
description:
Add a fourth backend to wolfP11 that turns a USB flash drive into a soft token by loading keys from an encrypted keystore file on the drive.

**What it does:**
On USB insertion (detected via existing libusb hotplug), wolfP11 scans the drive for supported key files and presents a new slot. On C_Login, the key file is decrypted and key material is loaded into mlock'd memory. On USB removal, key material is zeroized and the slot is marked token-absent.

**Threat model:**
Protects against disk theft and offline forensics. Keys never appear unencrypted on disk. Provides USB possession factor without requiring a hardware security token.

**Reference implementation:** ~/soft_PKCS11/usb-hsm — read for format specs, mlock/zeroize lifecycle, and PBKDF2 parameters. Do NOT copy Rust code; re-implement in C using wolfCrypt.

---

## Format dispatch table

The keystore loader dispatches on file header magic bytes/patterns BEFORE committing to a parse strategy. Every format reduces to the same internal Vec<wp11_key_entry_t> representation. Adding a new format touches only wp11_keystore.c — no changes to the backend, session, or PKCS#11 layer.

Header bytes / pattern                           Format                          Priority
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50 31 31 4B  ('P11K')                            .p11k native (wolfP11/usb-hsm)  P0 (must-have)
30 82 + PKCS#12 OID                              PKCS#12 (.pfx/.p12)             P1
30 82 + PBES2 OID / PKCS#8 unencrypted OID       DER PKCS#8 (any)                P1
'-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----'          PKCS#8 EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo  P1
'-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----'                    PKCS#8 unencrypted PEM          P1
'-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----'                Traditional RSA PEM (PKCS#1)    P1
'-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----'                 Traditional EC PEM (SEC1)       P1
'-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----'            OpenSSH new-format text         P2
6F 70 65 6E 73 73 68 2D 6B 65 79 2D 76 31 00   OpenSSH binary (openssh-key-v1) P2
'-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----'          OpenPGP armored (RFC 4880)      P2
C5/C7 packet tag                                 OpenPGP binary                  P2
'PuTTY-User-Key-File-2:' / '-3:'                PuTTY PPK v2/v3                 P3
FE ED FE ED                                      JKS Java KeyStore               P3
CE CE CE CE                                      JCEKS Java KeyStore             P3
'{' + '"private_key"'                          GCP Service Account JSON        P3

ASN.1 disambiguation: PKCS#12 vs PKCS#8 both start 0x30; distinguish by OID in first SEQUENCE:
- PKCS#12: OID 1.2.840.113549.1.12.10.1.x
- PKCS#8 PBES2: OID 1.2.840.113549.1.5.13
- PKCS#8 RSA: OID 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1
Never dispatch on file extension alone.

---

## .p11k wire format (v1 — P0)

[0..4]    magic: 'P11K'
[4]       version: 0x01
[5..37]   PBKDF2 salt (32 bytes, random)
[37..41]  PBKDF2 iterations (u32 BE; reject < 100,000)
[41..53]  AES-256-GCM nonce (12 bytes, random)
[53..57]  ciphertext length (u32 BE)
[57..]    AES-256-GCM ciphertext + 16-byte authentication tag
Ciphertext decrypts to CBOR-encoded array of key entries (id[16], label, key_type, DER bytes).

---

## Internal representation (all formats converge here)

typedef struct {
    uint8_t  id[16];        // CKA_ID
    char     label[64];     // CKA_LABEL
    int      key_type;      // WP11_KEY_RSA | WP11_KEY_EC | WP11_KEY_ED25519
    uint8_t *der_bytes;     // mlock'd allocation; zeroize-before-free
    size_t   der_len;
} wp11_key_entry_t;

---

## New files

- wolfp11/wp11_keystore.h    — format dispatch API, wp11_key_entry_t, error codes
- src/wp11_keystore.c        — format dispatch + .p11k parser (wolfCrypt AES-GCM, PBKDF2, mlock)
- src/wp11_backend_usb_flash.c — backend ops: sign/verify/decrypt dispatching into decrypted keys
- test/wp11_test_keystore.c  — .p11k parse/create tests with known test vectors (independent oracle)
- test/vectors/p11k_framing.json — hand-constructed test vectors, never generated from code under test

---

## Integration points

- wp11_backend.h: add WP11_BACKEND_USB_FLASH = 3
- wp11_settings.h: add WOLFP11_CFG_USB_FLASH_BACKEND compile-time guard
- wp11_pkcs11.c: C_Login for USB flash slots calls keystore decrypt; C_Logout and slot_remove call zeroize
- Makefile: USBFLASH=1 opt-in (like WOLFHSM=1)

---

## Key security requirements

- mlock key material immediately after decryption; munlock only after zeroize
- Zeroize with wolfCrypt ForceZero before free
- Reject .p11k with PBKDF2 iteration count below 100,000
- wolfCrypt RNG for salt/nonce generation
- No key material on the C stack; heap-allocate and track lifetime
- Unrecognized format returns WP11_KEYSTORE_ERR_UNSUPPORTED (not a fatal error)

---

## Acceptance criteria

- make USBFLASH=1 test passes clean
- .p11k round-trip: create keystore, load with correct PIN, load with wrong PIN
- C_Login decrypts keystore; C_Sign succeeds; wrong PIN returns CKR_PIN_INCORRECT
- USB removal zeroizes keys; subsequent C_Sign returns CKR_DEVICE_REMOVED
- Unknown file format returns CKR_TOKEN_NOT_RECOGNIZED (no crash, no partial parse)
- Tests use independent oracles (known PBKDF2+AES-GCM test vectors from external sources)
